scenario: Jul 31: Direct US-Iran exchanges widened after the five-day pause collapsed. US forces completed a two-hour heavy wave against dozens of IRGC command, missile, drone, coastal-surveillance and defence targets in response to Iran's attack on a US base in Jordan. Iran launched another regional barrage: Jordan intercepted five missiles for a second consecutive day, while a strike on a Chinese company's building in Kuwait killed one worker; Iranian media reported three killed and two wounded in US strikes on Qeshm Island (AP, Jul 30). Lloyd's List Intelligence data cited by AP show Hormuz traffic falling from 82 ships in Jul 13-19 to 39 in Jul 20-26. Brent was $88.00 (-0.41%, Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 31); TTF was 60.49 EUR/MWh (+3.83%, Yahoo Finance TTF=F, Jul 29); JKM's contextual CFD reference eased to $21.38/MMBtu (-0.26%, Trading Economics, Jul 30). The latest reviewed LNG-specific transit count remains the Jul 18 Kpler observation, and current route-normalised freight and war-risk costs remain unavailable. Tail raised to 70%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained by wartime-low Hormuz traffic. Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 39 ships in Jul 20-26, down from 82 the prior week. This sustains freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains, while Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September.
